title: Cache calibration velocity sync - Orchard Retail POC
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on observed KV/prefix cache hit rates. Reviewed metrics from last 7 days, identified prompt variability and per-tenant session IDs as main hit-rate blockers. Agreed on two immediate config changes (normalize user prompts, increase prefix TTL for carts), plan to run 72-hour targeted run with new configs and run a short canary on Dedicated vs Hosted routing. Security docs to be shared (SOC2 + KMS notes). Next call scheduled in one week.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-22
Start: 14:30 PDT
Duration: 45m
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Leah Ortiz (Redwood SE), Jenna Morris (Head of ML - Orchard), Carlos Vega (Eng Manager), Priya Nair (SRE), Ethan Brooks (Product)

Auto-generated Summary (may be imperfect):
Leah: walked through recent cache telemetry, prefix hit rate up slightly but KV hit plateaued. We talked about prompt variability and tenant ids. Action: normalization + tweak TTL for cart prefix.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Samir: All right, hey everybody thanks for joining. Quick check, can you hear me okay?
[00:06] Jenna: Yep, loud and clear.
[00:08] Carlos: good here.
[00:10] Samir: Cool. We're on for 45. Leah and I will run through the numbers and then we'll go into tuning items.
[00:18] Leah: Great. I'll share my screen in a sec. For context, this is the orchard-cart POC, week three of the KV/prefix caching experiment. We pulled last 7 days of telemetry, happy to talk through anomalies.
[00:30] [screen share noise]
[00:33] Leah: So slide one — overall token-level latency is stable, 95th at about 380ms on hosted routes. That's not new. The interesting part: prefix hit for cart flows is at 42% (up from 35%), KV hit is stuck at 18% unchanged.
[00:47] Jenna: Hmm. That KV number feels low, we expected better after the canonicalization from last week.
[00:52] Leah: Yeah we did some light normalization but the prompt set you sent had lots of per-session IDs and product variant strings. Those make keys explode.
[01:03] Ethan: So is the key space basically too sparse — each request is unique so the cache never reuses?
[01:07] Leah: Exactly. Two main vectors: one, session-scoped IDs appended to subject lines; two, micro variations in phrasing — e.g., 'what's in my cart' vs 'show my cart items' produce different prefixes.
[01:18] Carlos: We saw that too — our frontend adds a 6-char truncated UUID to track devices and some of that leaks into the prompt. We thought Redwood's prefix logic would ignore it.
[01:27] Leah: The prefix rules are conservative by default; they don't drop arbitrary tokens unless you tell them to canonicalize. We can add a tenant strip and a regex to drop these UUID patterns on the KV key derivation.
[01:37] Priya: Any risk to changing keystuff? We need to preserve auditability and not break correlation for logs.
[01:44] Samir: Good call. Leah — can you speak to audit logs and correlation ids? If we canonicalize, do we preserve a mapping in logs?
[01:50] Leah: Yes — we will keep the original string in the request metadata and only transform the key used for the cache. Audit logs still contain the raw user input and the derived cache key, so you can trace. Also, KMS remains the same — no plaintext keying change.
[02:05] Jenna: OK that helps. Back to the numbers — are there specific flows that are high value for hitting?
[02:11] Leah: Cart preview, quick-price-check, and returns estimate are top. Cart preview has higher temporal locality so raising TTL helps. Right now cart prefix TTL is 60s, we suggest 300s for cart preview window.
[02:24] Carlos: Four minutes — that would definitely up the hit rate during quick browse sessions. What's the eviction policy now? LRU?
[02:30] Leah: It's an LRU with session affinity heuristics. But since your traffic pattern has spikes during promos, we can bias towards keeping cart prefixes warm by tagging them as 'hot' for an extra cooling period.
[02:41] Samir: Quick check on cost: increasing TTL increases memory pressure — Leah any rough unit economics impact?
[02:46] Leah: Small bump. For your scale, we've modeled a 7% increase in GPU memory usage but a 12% drop in per-request p99 token cost due to fewer recompute calls. Net cost goes down for cart-heavy pages. We'll put numbers in the spreadsheet.
[03:00] Jenna: Nice.
[03:02] Ethan: You mentioned prefetch heuristics earlier — can you expand?
[03:05] Leah: Sure — for flows like add-to-cart we can prefetch likely-needed prefixes when a user takes an earlier action. Example: when they open product page, prefetch cart summary for that session id. Prefetch is best-effort and can be throttled to avoid noise.
[03:19] Carlos: We're worried prefetch plus our peak traffic might blow up backend calls. Can prefetch be limited to a small pool?
[03:25] Leah: Yes, rate-limited and percentage-based. We can also only prefetch for users with history above threshold.
[03:31] Priya: Is prefetch charged as regular inference calls? How do we measure ROI?
[03:36] Samir: Yes prefetch is a call; ROI measured as hit uplift vs prefetch cost. Leah will run an ROI calc in the benchmark sheet.
[03:44] Leah: I'll add a prefetch ROI tab.
[03:46] [short pause]
[03:50] Jenna: Quick yes/no — does Redwood support per-tenant keyspaces so one tenant can't evict another's hot items?
[03:57] Leah: We do. You can set shard isolation (dedicated caches per tenant) on Dedicated capacity, or logical tags on Hosted. There's a small overhead for per-tenant isolation on Hosted, we can scope that in the doc.
[04:09] Carlos: For our POC we want logical isolation on Hosted for now. If Dedicated yields big wins we'll consider switching.
[04:16] Samir: Sounds sensible. We'll plan a small canary to route 5% of your peak-hour traffic to Dedicated and compare p95/p99 and unit cost.
[04:25] Ethan: Timeline for that?
[04:27] Samir: If SRE signs off, we can do it next Wednesday during your mid-day window.
[04:33] Priya: I'll try to schedule the smoke test on Monday and confirm.
[04:36] Jenna: Back to normalization — what regex patterns do you recommend for our common leaks?
[04:41] Leah: Strip device uuids (hex sequences 6-12 chars), strip ISO timestamps, normalize numeric variants (e.g., 8 -> <NUM>), collapse common synonyms with a mapping (like show my cart -> cart summary). We can ship a default set and you can add custom rules.
[04:57] Carlos: How do we test new rules without affecting production?
[05:00] Leah: We have a staging keyspace. We'll instrument a dry-run mode where we compute transformed keys and log the delta. That gives you metrics on potential hit-rate uplift before committing.
[05:10] Jenna: Perfect. We'll feed you the prompt set so you can run dry-run against it.
[05:14] Leah: Great. I put that as an action.
[05:17] [10 second silence]
[05:27] Samir: Let's surface one anomaly — on Apr 19th at 14:00 we saw a KV eviction storm correlated to a product feed job. Any detail?
[05:35] Priya: yeah that is ours — we run a nightly product sync which on that day had a bad loop and regenerated millions of product variants which spilled into user prompts.
[05:44] Leah: That explains the spike. For cases like product feed noise, we recommend filtering those heavy backfills from cache key derivation or rate-limiting background processes.
[05:55] Carlos: We'll add rules to ignore ingest pipeline variants.
[05:58] Ethan: On the security front — Jenna had a question about KMS and audit logs earlier. Jenna, want us to loop back?
[06:04] Jenna: Yes. We need to ensure any normalization doesn't remove evidence for audits. Also want to see the SOC 2 docs and whether Redwood does customer-managed keys.
[06:13] Samir: Short answers: audits preserved in logs, and we support both Redwood-managed KMS and customer-managed KMS via HSM integrations for Private deployments. I'll send the SOC2 excerpt and KMS note after this call.
[06:25] Jenna: Thanks.
[06:27] Leah: Another tuning item: prefix window size. We currently consider the first N tokens (N=64) as prefix. For cart prompts which are smaller, reducing N to 32 reduces noisy tokens included in the prefix. I'd recommend N=32 for cart flows and keep N=64 for conversation-like flows.
[06:45] Carlos: Does that change impact streaming behavior?
[06:48] Leah: Very little. It's a pre-key derivation step. If you use streaming you'll see the same outputs; it's only the cache key derivation that changes.
[06:54] Jenna: So to recap the concrete config changes we want to try: 1) prompt normalization rules (regex/num collapse), 2) tenant/device UUID strip, 3) prefix TTL to 300s for cart previews, 4) reduce prefix N to 32 for cart flows. Does that sound right?
[07:08] Leah: Yes. We'll also add a dry-run on staging and a prefetch ROI calc.
[07:13] Samir: I'll note that down. Jenna — can you confirm who will own the sample prompt set?
[07:18] Jenna: I'll send it today, aiming before EOD.
[07:21] Samir: Great.
[07:24] [pause while Samir types]
[07:30] Leah: Quick note on metrics instrumentation — we added a token-level trace where you can attribute tokens to cache misses. It surfaces the top 10 token patterns causing misses.
[07:41] Carlos: That will be super helpful. Can we get a weekly export instead of manual queries?
[07:46] Leah: Yes, we'll enable a scheduled export to your S3 bucket. Need an ARN and minimum permissions.
[07:53] Priya: We'll send the ARN.
[07:56] [small cross talk]
[08:00] Ethan: Any concerns about privacy with token-level tracing? We have PII rules.
[08:05] Leah: Traces can be PII-redacted. We can apply a redaction pipeline before storing and still compute patterns. We'll share the redaction config.
[08:14] Jenna: Good.
[08:16] Samir: Ok a couple org-level asks: could you confirm target success criteria for the POC? Jenna earlier mentioned hit-rate uplift and cost per query drop. Jenna, do you have numbers?
[08:27] Jenna: Target is +20 percentage points on KV hit (so from 18% to 38%) and at least 10% reduction in per-request cost while keeping p95 latency within 10% of current. If we hit that within 30 days, we move to procurement.
[08:42] Samir: Understood — we'll aim for that and put checkpoints.
[08:46] Leah: Also flag: some of the gains are non-linear with Dedicated; Dedicated offers per-tenant isolation and larger memory pools which can push KV hit higher. We'll capture both hosted and dedicated performance during the canary.
[08:59] Carlos: Cost difference ballpark?
[09:02] Leah: Dedicated has a fixed footprint and lower per-token variable cost at scale. For your current traffic estimate, Dedicated is roughly 18% cheaper at the p50 cost but has a monthly commit. We'll include a model.
[09:15] Jenna: We'll evaluate the economics if the hit-rate target is achievable.
[09:19] [brief pause]
[09:22] Samir: OK let's run through action items quick. Leah will push normalization rules in staging and run dry-run. Jenna to send prompt set. Priya to run smoke test. Samir to send SOC2 and KMS notes and benchmark template. Any additions?
[09:36] Priya: I'll also run the Dedicated canary capacity test if we greenlight.
[09:40] Samir: Perfect.
[09:42] Ethan: A couple of questions from product: if we canonicalize a prompt, will we ever see false positives where two different intents map to same key?
[09:51] Leah: Good question. There's a tradeoff. We try to canonicalize only noise tokens and not intent tokens. But we will generate a collision risk report in dry-run mode so you can see potential false merges.
[10:04] Jenna: If we see collisions, can we whitelist intent markers to stay distinct?
[10:08] Leah: Yes, you can add keep tokens. That's part of the customization.
[10:12] [pause]
[10:20] Samir: Security quick pulse — Jenna wants SOC2 and KMS note, we'll also include RBAC and audit log retention policy. Anything else security should see?
[10:30] Priya: Encryption in transit and at rest details, and SSO/SAML integration flow.
[10:35] Samir: We'll include that.
[10:37] [short silence]
[10:41] Leah: OK technical checklist to deliver: 1) normalization rule set deployed to staging (dry-run enabled), 2) prefix TTL update for cart, 3) prefix N changes for cart, 4) prefetch ROI tab + scheduled token trace export to S3.
[10:58] Jenna: Sounds good.
[11:00] Samir: Anything else from Orchard side?
[11:03] Carlos: We'll check the product feed pipeline to make sure backfills don't leak.
[11:07] Ethan: I'll document user flow priority.
[11:10] Jenna: I'll review the benchmark targets and confirm.
[11:13] Samir: Great. Let's lock the next sync — same time next week?
[11:16] Jenna: Works for me.
[11:18] Priya: Works.
[11:20] Samir: Awesome. Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with notes and the docs.
[11:25] [meeting ends]

Notes about transcription: occasional word swaps and names may be imperfect (e.g., KV cache heard as KV cash). Also timestamps approximate.
